items.title: CTM360 Exposes Fake Gift Card Scams Exploiting Trusted Brands
items.description: Scammers are impersonating major brands and celebrities to lure consumers into fake gift card giveaways that collect personal information and trigger unwanted subscriptions. CTM360 reveals how these campaigns use deceptive verification steps and affiliate networks to generate revenue without delivering the promised rewards. [...]

items.title: SonicWall Warns of Potential In-the-Wild Exploitation of SSLVPN Flaw That Bypasses MFA
items.description: SonicWall has warned customers to patch a SonicOS SSLVPN vulnerability that could let attackers bypass SAML authentication and its multi-factor authentication checks. Tracked as CVE-2026-19868, the flaw carries a CVSS score of 7.1. The company has investigated a report indicating potential exploitation and strongly urges customers to upgrade promptly. The issue affects SSLVPN only when […] The…

items.title: SonicWall Patches Exploited SonicOS Vulnerability That Weakens VPN Logins
items.description: CVE-2026-19868 can let attackers holding credentials for a different login method get past SAML checks, including SAML-enforced MFA. The post SonicWall Patches Exploited SonicOS Vulnerability That Weakens VPN Logins appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Claude Code’s “Yes, and Don’t Ask Again” Option Can Leak Passwords and API Keys to GitHub
items.description: Claude Code’s “Yes, and don’t ask again” option can save passwords and API keys inside project settings that later reach public GitHub repositories. Apiiro researchers found 2,539 distinct secrets across 1,994 public repositories, showing how a routine approval can turn private credentials into public data. The research identified 63 affected organizations, mostly software companies. Exposed […]…

items.title: Claude Code's “Don't Ask Again” File Exposes Passwords and Keys in 1,122 Public Copies on GitHub
items.description: Passwords and API keys that developers typed into commands they approved in Claude Code are sitting in public GitHub repositories, where anyone can read them.
